@@U03655@@
Our mountains, our cities, our shores and sea are pleasing to him, the god, and are lovely and bright. We have no fogs or mist, no sunless haze, and should one steal upon us, a beam of sun and a breeze clears us of these, and the island is once again bright. From on high he sees himself, your brother god, in a hundred statues, as a youth, a giant, now great, now gentle. We were the first, you know, in all the world, to cast the gods in the noble form of man.

@@U03657@@
(To 荷蒙库鲁斯,)

@@U03658@@
Let them sing, let them boast. To the sacred life-giving rays of the sun such lifeless things are nothing. They go on sculpting, casting, endlessly, and once they have it in bronze they think they've really got something. And what comes of all this pride in the end? These godly statues stand there so grand— and an earthquake destroys them. They've been melted down long since. What is this earthly life, even at its best, but a weariness of the flesh! The sea is the proper element for life. I'll be 普罗透斯-Dolphin now, and carry you into the eternal waters.

@@U03659@@
(He transforms himself.)

@@U03660@@
There, that’s done. Up on my back, now.
translation:
@@U03655@@
我们的山峦、我们的城市、我们的海岸和海洋都令上帝喜悦，而且可爱而明亮。我们没有雾气，没有没有阳光的薄雾，如果有人悄悄靠近我们，一束阳光和一阵微风就会清除我们的这些，岛上再次变得明亮。他从高处看到自己，你的兄弟神，在一百尊雕像中，作为一个年轻人，一个巨人，现​​在伟大，现在温柔。你知道，我们是世界上第一个将诸神塑造成高贵的人形的人。

@@U03657@@
（致荷蒙库鲁斯）

@@U03658@@
让他们歌唱，让他们夸耀。对于赋予生命的神圣阳光来说，这些无生命的东西根本算不了什么。他们没完没了地继续雕刻、铸造，一旦他们把它变成青铜，他们就认为自己真的得到了一些东西。所有这些骄傲最终会带来什么？这些神圣的雕像矗立在那里，如此宏伟——一场地震将它们摧毁了。它们早已被融化了。尘世的生活，即使在最好的时候，也只不过是肉体的疲倦而已！海洋是生命最适宜的元素。现在我将成为普罗透斯-海豚，带你进入永恒的水域。

@@U03659@@
（他改变了自己。）

@@U03660@@
到了这里，就完成了。现在，在我的背上。
